sent_subject: Ember Yoga homepage teardown: the blocker to fix today + the quickest wins
sent:
Priya,

Your public domain (emberyoga.co.uk) is currently showing a Squarespace “Website Expired” page. Until that’s fixed, paid and organic visitors can’t see the intro offer or book.

Do these in order:

Today
- Restore the site (Squarespace subscription/domain/DNS) and pause paid until live.
- Put a simple fallback page live: studio picker, intro offer summary and terms, one “Book first class” CTA per studio, phone number, opening hours. Link it from each Google Business Profile so searchers can still book.
- Check that conversion tracking still fires on the booking confirmation page.

This week
- Replace the generic hero (“Find your calm in the city”) with an intent headline tied to location and the intro offer, plus a single CTA. Example: “Start yoga at [Studio name] — flexible timetable for beginners. Book your first class.”
- Above the fold: studio selector (or detect nearest), today/tomorrow timetable toggle, intro-offer price and key terms (who it’s for, duration, renewal), and one CTA.
- Social proof: surface 3–5 recent Google reviews per studio near the CTA; show overall rating.
- Reduce anxiety: “What to bring”, heat level, beginner-friendly badge, cancellation policy snippet.
- Light urgency: show the next two beginner-friendly class times with seat status (e.g., Filling fast) instead of a countdown timer.
- Create per‑studio “Intro offer” pages and send paid traffic to them. One promise, one page. This is the studio equivalent of what lifted conversion for Tallow & Thyme (4.8% vs 1.9%) and cut cost per first order 38% for Oatside Kitchen.

Booking flow
- Pre‑select studio and “Intro offer” in step one; minimise fields until after slot choice.
- Keep the user in one view; keep price visible; show total time to book.
- Confirmation: add‑to‑calendar, how to get there, facilities.

Speed and mobile
- Compress hero images, defer non‑essential scripts, and lazy‑load maps; target sub‑2.5s to first paint on 4G.
- Make the CTA thumb‑reachable; de‑emphasise header links on mobile.

What to measure
- Intro‑offer purchases and first‑class bookings per 100 visits, by studio page.
- Click‑through from hero to “Book first class” and drop‑off between studio page and booking step one.

If it helps, I can sketch a quick wireframe for one studio page based on this.

Fieldwork Studio
